issues.description:
Method: Milkable.messageOnMilk
- Problem statement (UML and Part 2 instructions) and the template Main expect a no-argument method messageOnMilk() that returns a String and state the return should be of the form "[Animal Type] [name] is milked".
- Solution defines the interface method as messageOnMilk(double volume) (i.e. it requires a double parameter) and the Seal and Goat implementations implement messageOnMilk(double) returning strings that include the volume (e.g. "Seal X is milked (1.0L)").
- This is a parameter-list mismatch: the problem and template call messageOnMilk() with no arguments, but the solution requires a double argument. Students following the problem/template will implement and call a no-argument method; the solution's signature will not match that expectation and will cause confusion and potential compilation issues when integrating or testing implementations against the described API.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the Milkable API consistent across all artifacts. Two viable options:
1) Align solution to the problem/template: change the solution interface to `String messageOnMilk()` (no parameters) and update Seal and Goat to implement `messageOnMilk()` returning exactly "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". Also update any solution code that currently uses the volume parameter.
2) If a volume parameter is intentionally required, update the problem statement (UML and Part 2 text), the template Main usage (calls to messageOnMilk), and any tests to require `messageOnMilk(double volume)` and document how the volume should appear in the returned string. Prefer option 1 to preserve the original exercise wording and to match the current template usage.

issues.description: Concept: the Milkable.messageOnMilk operation (milking an animal). Problem statement (UML and textual instructions) and the template usage treat it as a parameterless method messageOnMilk():String (e.g., UML lines 51-53 and instructions in Part 2 which say messageOnMilk() should return "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). The template Main.java calls m.messageOnMilk() with no arguments. The solution repository defines a different signature: Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java) and implements it in Goat and Seal with a double parameter and return strings that include the volume. This is an identifier/signature inconsistency: the same conceptual method has different signatures across artifacts. Students following the problem statement or template will expect a no-argument method; the solution API requires a double parameter, causing compilation mismatch and confusion about the required implementation and return format.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable.messageOnMilk signature consistent across all artifacts. Recommended (minimal change to align with problem statement and template): change the solution API to a parameterless method: in solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java declare String messageOnMilk(); then update Goat and Seal to implement messageOnMilk() returning "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (no volume). Alternative (if volume is intended): update the problem statement UML, the Part 2 instructions, and the template Main.java to require messageOnMilk(double volume), showing example calls with a volume and specifying the return format (e.g., "Seal Clarabelle is milked (1.5L)"); then keep the solution as-is. Ensure all three places (problem statement/UML, template code, and solution) use the same signature and example return format.
